metadata.title: Network Core

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for Network and Connectivity Services establishing baseline institutional connectivity and trust boundaries.

props.name: technology-platform
props.remarks: Core network infrastructure, routing, and switching platforms.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Managed institutional network fabric with explicit trust boundaries.

props.name: data-entity
props.remarks: Network address, topology, and connectivity metadata.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Network Core provides transport connectivity without establishing implicit trust based on network location, consistent with Zero Trust Architecture principles.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Core network services support identity-aware and policy-driven enforcement implemented by dependent Secure Network patterns.

metadata.remarks:
Network Core defines the foundational capability that establishes what it means for systems, devices, and services to be connected to the institutional network. It defines baseline addressability, routing, reachability, and trust boundaries independent of access control, segmentation, inspection, policy mediation, or resiliency mechanisms.

Governance and Responsibility Anchor:
This pattern is the authoritative anchor for SSPPs, standards, procedures, and assurance related to institutional network connectivity. Threat and defense considerations are intentionally expressed at the capability level to allow precise assurance of core behavior without embedding policy or control logic into the core transport layer.

components.title: Addressability
components.description: Assignment and management of network addresses and identifiers to enable controlled reachability.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Network service discovery enabled by overly permissive addressability.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Restriction of addressability reduces unauthorized discovery.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Control network addressability to enforce boundaries and limit exposure.

components.title: Routing and Forwarding
components.description: Controlled routing and forwarding of network traffic based on defined topology and governance.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Traffic manipulation through compromised or misconfigured routing.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Enforced routing policies prevent unauthorized path redirection.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Ensure routing and forwarding mechanisms enforce defined network paths.

components.title: Trust Boundaries
components.description: Definition and enforcement of institutional network trust boundaries.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Lateral movement across weak or unenforced network trust boundaries.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Explicit enforcement of trust boundaries limits unauthorized cross-domain traffic.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Define and enforce network trust boundaries between security domains.

components.title: Baseline Connectivity
components.description: Establishment of minimum, approved connectivity paths required for institutional operations.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Abuse of permitted baseline application protocols for covert command-and-control or data movement.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Restricting baseline connectivity reduces abuse of always-allowed network paths.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Allow only essential network services and connectivity paths.
